transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hey, yeah, thanks. So, what brings me in... well, it's mostly work stuff. I supervise a sales team now, and I just keep making these really dumb mistakes on our sales reports. Like, I'll be copying the wrong numbers over from the team dashboard. 

Which is honestly so frustrating because I've been in sales since right out of high school. I actually started out selling those massive water filtration systems door-to-door. Man, my buddy Mike and I used to lug those heavy things around in his beat-up Chevy. The AC in that car was completely shot, so we'd just be sweating through our ties all summer. We used to stop at this little gas station on Route 9 just to stand in the beer cooler for five minutes... 

But anyway, what was I—oh, right, the reports. Yeah, so at my job now, I'll be checking over a procedure I'm supposed to review, and I'll just completely miss a line. And the crazy part is, I do check it. Even when I thought I went over the whole thing and double-checked it, the mistake is still there. It's like my eyes just skip right past it. Kind of like how I completely missed the expiration date on my milk this morning and ruined a perfectly good bowl of cereal. Have you ever done that? It really just ruins your whole morning.
Do you find yourself making these kinds of mistakes in other areas of your life, outside of work?

Outside of work? Um... I'm not really sure, honestly. I don't think so? I mean, I don't really have a lot of paperwork or data stuff at home to mess up. Usually, when I'm off the clock, I'm just trying to unwind, you know? 

Like this past weekend, I decided I was finally going to fix up my back deck. The wood was getting all warped from all that rain we had last month. My neighbor, Dave, he's got all these crazy expensive power tools he never uses because he's a dentist and I swear he's terrified of cutting a finger off. Which makes sense, I guess, you kind of need your hands to fix teeth. But anyway, he let me borrow his power washer, and man, power washing is so satisfying. Have you ever watched those videos online where they just blast the grime off a driveway? I could watch those for hours, it's just... mesmerizing. 

But wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, mistakes at home. Yeah, no, nothing really comes to mind like the work reports. I don't really notice anything like that if I do.
Do you often find yourself forgetting things that happened recently?

Forgetting recent things? Um, no, not really. I feel like my memory for that kind of stuff is actually pretty sharp. Like, I can tell you exactly what happened yesterday down to the minute. I actually went to this new deli for lunch, the one they just built where the old Blockbuster used to be over on 4th street. 

Man, do you remember Blockbuster? I kind of miss it, honestly. There was something about just walking the aisles on a Friday night, trying to pick a movie just by looking at the cardboard covers. My older brother and I used to rent those terrible, cheesy B-horror movies all the time. We got this one about giant mutant spiders once, and the special effects were so unbelievably bad, you could literally see the fishing line holding up the plastic spider legs. My brother actually tried to build his own giant spider out of pipe cleaners and black duct tape after that to scare our mom. He hid it in the laundry basket, and she screamed so loud the dog started howling... 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, forgetting things. Yeah, no, I don't really have an issue with that. Recent stuff usually sticks in my head just fine.
Do you have trouble focusing on tasks for long periods of time?

Focusing for long periods? Um... I don't know, I guess I've never really thought about it like that. I mean, I can focus if it's something I'm really into. But if it's boring? Yeah, maybe it's a little tough. 

Like, we have these quarterly review meetings at work, right? And they just drag on forever. Our regional director, Tom, he loves the sound of his own voice. He'll just go on and on about synergistic paradigms or whatever corporate buzzword he learned that week. I swear, last time he talked for forty-five minutes straight about "leveraging cross-functional bandwidth." I spent the whole time trying to figure out if his tie was slightly crooked or if one of his shoulders was just higher than the other. I'm pretty sure it's the shoulder. He probably carries his golf clubs on that side. He's obsessed with golf. He actually invited me to play once, but honestly, I don't get the appeal. You just hit a little ball and then walk after it for four hours. I'd rather be doing something fast-paced, you know? Like go-karting. Have you ever been to that indoor track off I-95? Those things go surprisingly fast, like, you actually have to brake for the corners or you'll spin out...

Wait, sorry, what was the question? Oh, focusing. Yeah, I don't know, I guess I haven't really noticed a huge problem with it, unless it's just something super boring like Tom's meetings.
Do you often find your mind wandering away from what you're doing?

Mind wandering? Yeah, I guess that happens a lot, actually. Like, when I'm trying to review call notes or crunch the numbers for my team, it doesn't take much. Just one conversation across the room, or even a random thought about something I need to do at home, and suddenly I'm completely off track before I even realize it. 

Like yesterday, I was right in the middle of checking the sales logs, and I heard Jimmy—he's one of my newer guys—talking about his fantasy football draft. He took a kicker in the fourth round. The fourth round! I mean, who does that? Kickers are basically a dime a dozen, you can grab one off the waiver wire in week three and be totally fine. I spent like twenty minutes mentally restructuring his entire roster because it was just bothering me so much. I used to be huge into fantasy football, actually won my league back in 2018. We had this giant, ridiculous trophy with a plastic armchair on top. My wife hated it, she made me keep it in the garage...

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, my mind wandering. Yeah, so, like I was saying, it happens pretty easily when I'm trying to look at the numbers and stuff.
Do you feel overwhelmed or anxious when you make these mistakes at work?

Overwhelmed or anxious about mistakes? Um... no, not really. I mean, I don't really get anxious about it. It's just part of the job, you know? 

Like, if I mess up a number on a report, I just fix it. It's not a huge deal. Usually, my manager, Dave, catches it anyway. Dave's got this eagle eye for spreadsheets. It's actually kind of annoying. He'll just stand behind my desk, drinking out of this massive Yeti cup he has. It's one of those really big ones, like, I think it holds 64 ounces or something crazy. He puts these weird stickers all over it. He's got one from some microbrewery in Vermont, and another one that's just a picture of a sloth wearing sunglasses. I asked him about the sloth once, and he said it was his "spirit animal." Which is hilarious, because Dave is the most high-strung guy I know. He drinks like six cups of coffee before noon. I don't even know how he sleeps at night. I tried drinking that much coffee once when we were doing inventory, and I felt like my heart was going to vibrate right out of my chest. I had to go walk laps around the parking lot just to burn off the energy. It was freezing out, too, middle of January...

Wait, sorry, what was the question? Oh, anxious about mistakes. Yeah, no, I don't really feel overwhelmed by them or anything. I just deal with it and move on.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety?

Restless? Yeah, definitely. I mean, especially if I'm stuck sitting somewhere. Like I was saying about Tom's meetings—sitting through those long ones, it honestly feels like my body is just buzzing inside. Like I can't just be still. I'm always shifting around in my chair, tapping my foot, clicking a pen, whatever. Half the time I just make up an excuse to get up and go to the bathroom or grab water just so I can move. 

Actually, the water cooler on our floor is the worst. It's one of those old ones where the hot water button is sticky, so you have to press it really hard, and then it kind of shoots out at an angle. Jimmy burned his hand on it last week. He was trying to make oatmeal or something. I don't know why he eats oatmeal at 2 PM, but he does. He brings these little packets of the dinosaur egg oatmeal, you know the ones? Where the little sugar eggs melt into dinosaurs when you add hot water? I used to love those when I was a kid. My mom would only buy them if they were on sale, though. She was super strict about the grocery budget. She had this whole coupon binder system, like, color-coded and everything. It was intense. She'd spend hours on Sunday mornings clipping coupons from the newspaper... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, feeling fidgety. Yeah, so, like sitting still in meetings is just really hard, I get all buzzy and have to move around.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Act on impulse? Hmm, I don't really think so. I mean, I don't feel like I just do stuff without thinking. I usually try to figure things out first, you know? 

Like, when I'm looking at the sales territories, I don't just assign people randomly. I try to match them up based on who's good at what. Like, Sarah is great with the tech clients, so I put her out west. She actually just bought a new house out there, near the mountains. It's gorgeous. She showed me pictures on her phone. They have this huge deck in the back, and they're talking about putting in a hot tub. I told her she has to be careful with hot tubs, though, because the maintenance is a nightmare. My neighbor, Gary, he got one last summer, and he spends half his weekend just checking the pH levels and dumping chemicals in it. He's got this whole shed just full of chlorine and stuff. It smells like a public pool every time I walk out to get my mail. Gary's a good guy, though. He helped me fix my lawnmower last spring when the carburetor got all gunked up. He used to be a mechanic before he retired, so he knows everything about small engines. We spent like three hours in his garage, just tinkering with it, and he was telling me all these crazy stories about the shop he used to run...

Wait, sorry. Impulse, right? Yeah, no, I don't really think I have a problem with that. I try to think things through.
Do you find it hard to pay attention to details when working on a task for a long time?

Pay attention to details? Yeah, actually, that's kind of what brings me in. I keep making these really dumb mistakes on our sales reports. Like, I'll be copying numbers over from the team dashboard, and I just put the wrong ones down, or I'll completely miss a line in a procedure I was supposed to check off, even when I thought I went over the whole thing. 

It's just so frustrating because I know the dashboard like the back of my hand. The IT guys just updated it, actually. They changed the whole color scheme to this weird neon green and dark grey. It's supposed to be "easier on the eyes," but honestly, it just makes me feel like I'm looking at the Matrix. You know that movie? With Keanu Reeves? I watched that again a few weeks ago. It still holds up, honestly. The special effects were so ahead of their time. My buddy Mike, he used to be obsessed with it. He actually bought one of those long black leather trench coats back in high school. He wore it every day, even when it was like ninety degrees out. We used to give him so much crap for it. He works in insurance now, up in Albany. He's got three kids, and he drives a minivan, so I guess the trench coat days are long gone. We went fishing up there last summer, and he was telling me about how expensive braces are... 

Sorry, I'm doing it again. What was the question? Oh, details. Yeah, I struggle with the details on those reports, making silly errors even when I try to check my work.
Do you think you would make the same mistakes on the sales reports if someone was standing over your shoulder, guiding you through it?

If someone was standing right over my shoulder? Hmm, honestly, I think I'd still mess it up. Like I said, that's really what brings me in—I just keep making these dumb mistakes on the sales reports. Even if I'm trying to be super careful or someone's watching, I still end up copying the wrong numbers from the team dashboard, or I'll just completely miss a line in a procedure I was supposed to check off. And I always think I went over the whole thing perfectly.

It's like my brain just skips over things. Kind of like when you're driving home and you don't remember the last three miles. I do that all the time on the interstate. Route 95 is the worst for that, especially past exit 14. They've been doing construction there for, what, three years now? It's ridiculous. They put up all those orange barrels, and then nobody actually works on it. My uncle Tony used to work for the highway department, driving one of those massive dump trucks. He said half the time they're just waiting on permits or materials, so they just leave the cones out. Tony's retired now, though. He moved down to Florida, bought a condo in Boca. He plays pickleball like every single day. I guess pickleball is huge down there. He tried to explain the rules to me over Thanksgiving, but it just sounds like giant ping-pong. He actually tore his meniscus playing last month. Had to get surgery and everything. They gave him this crazy brace that looks like something out of Terminator...

Wait, sorry. The reports. Yeah, even with someone watching, I still make those same dumb mistakes, like copying the wrong numbers or missing steps. It's just really frustrating.
Do you have trouble organizing your tasks or workspace?

Organizing my tasks or workspace? No, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I have trouble with it. I've got a system that works for me, you know? I keep my desk pretty straightforward. 

Like, I have this one spot for the incoming contracts, and then a tray for the ones I need to review. I actually bought that tray at this little antique shop my wife dragged me to a couple of weekends ago. It's solid oak, really heavy. The guy running the shop said it was from an old post office from the 1920s. He had all this wild stuff in there—like, old brass diving helmets, a taxidermy bear that looked like it had seen better days. My wife ended up buying this vintage mirror with a really ornate gold frame. We spent like two hours trying to figure out how to hang it in the hallway because the drywall in our house is so cheap. We had to go to Home Depot to get special anchors. The guy at Home Depot, Dave, he was super helpful. He actually recommended a specific drill bit, too. I always go to Dave when I'm there. He's got this massive beard, looks like a lumberjack, but he knows everything about hardware. He was telling me he's building a cabin up in Maine on the weekends. Just driving up there every Friday night, sleeping in a tent, and building this place from scratch. Sounds exhausting, honestly, but he says it's peaceful. He's got a wood-burning stove picked out and everything...

Sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, organizing. Yeah, no, my workspace is fine. I don't really have any issues keeping my stuff in order.
Do you think you could avoid making these mistakes if you really tried?

If I really tried? Honestly, I feel like I *am* trying. That's the whole reason I'm here, you know? I just keep making these dumb mistakes on the sales reports, no matter how hard I try to focus. I'll be copying numbers from the team dashboard, and I just put down the wrong ones, or I'll miss a whole line on a procedure checklist. And the crazy part is, I always think I went over the whole thing perfectly. 

I'll sit there, staring at the screen, and it's like my brain just decides to take a break. Kind of like when my dog, Buster, just stops walking in the middle of a walk. He's a golden retriever mix, and he's got this thing where if he sees a squirrel, he just freezes. Like, completely statuesque. We'll be halfway around the block, and suddenly I'm dragging a fifty-pound anchor. My wife thinks it's hilarious, but she's not the one standing in the freezing cold at six in the morning waiting for him to snap out of it. We got him from this rescue down in Virginia. They drove him all the way up here in this big transport van with like thirty other dogs. The lady driving the van was telling us she does that trip every weekend. Just non-stop driving. She had this huge thermos of coffee that looked like it belonged on a construction site. I don't know how she drinks that much caffeine and still sits still for twelve hours. I can't even drink one cup after noon or I'm up all night staring at the ceiling. 

Anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, trying harder. Yeah, I don't think trying harder is the issue. I really do try to check my work, but I still end up missing those lines or copying the wrong numbers. It's driving me crazy.
Do you have trouble managing your emotions when something frustrating happens?

Managing my emotions? No, I wouldn't say I have trouble with that. I mean, I get annoyed like anyone else, but I don't blow up or anything. I'm pretty even-keeled, mostly. 

Like yesterday, we had this massive server outage at work right in the middle of the afternoon. Everyone was freaking out because the quarterly numbers are due on Friday, and the system was just totally locked up. I just went down to the breakroom to grab a snack while they fixed it. They actually just restocked the vending machine with those jalapeno kettle chips. I love those things. I used to buy them in bulk from this warehouse club near my old apartment, but then they stopped carrying them for some reason. Replaced them with this weird baked veggie chip thing that tasted like cardboard. My buddy Mark tried to convince me they were healthier, but he eats like a rabbit anyway. He's doing that raw food diet thing. I don't get it. He literally brought a Tupperware container full of raw broccoli and almonds to a football watch party last weekend. We were all eating wings and pizza, and he's just crunching away in the corner. The game was terrible, by the way. Our defense completely fell apart in the fourth quarter. The coach kept calling these ridiculous blitz packages when we should have just dropped into coverage... 

Wait, sorry. Emotions. Yeah, no, I handle frustration fine. I just kind of roll with it.
Do you feel like you're putting in enough effort when working on the sales reports?

Enough effort? Yeah, absolutely. I mean, I really am trying my best on them. I sit down, I block out the time, I'm putting the work in. It's just... I don't know. 

Part of it is the system we use for those reports, it's just so outdated anyway. Our IT guy, Greg, he's supposed to be upgrading it next month. He actually just got back from this massive comic convention out in San Diego. He was showing me pictures in the breakroom—he spent like six months building this crazy suit of armor out of foam and LED lights for it. His whole garage is basically a prop workshop now. I was telling my brother about it, because my brother used to build those remote-control airplanes. You know, the ones that smell like that intense model glue? We used to take them to the park when we were kids. One time he got this really expensive one stuck in the top of a huge oak tree, and my dad tried to knock it down with a pool skimmer. Ended up hitting a hornet's nest instead. Man, I have never seen my dad run so fast in my life. He lost one of his flip-flops in the grass and just kept going... 

Sorry, I lost my train of thought. Effort on the reports. Yeah, I don't know what else I can do, honestly. I feel like I'm putting in all the effort I have, it's just not working out right.
Do you find it hard to motivate yourself to start tasks, even when you know they need to be done?

Motivate myself to start? No, not really. I mean, if something needs to be done, I just do it. I don't sit around dreading it or anything. Like, if I know I have to mow the lawn, I just go get the mower. 

Though, honestly, my mower has been acting up lately. It's this old Toro I bought off a guy on Craigslist like five years ago. Started making this horrible grinding noise last weekend. I probably just need to change the oil or clean the spark plug, but I was looking at those new electric mowers at Home Depot. They're so quiet now. My neighbor, Dave, got one of those robotic ones that just drives around by itself. It looks like a little green Roomba for the yard. It's kind of creepy, actually, watching it just silently crawl around his front lawn at dusk. His wife hates it because she says it runs over her petunias, but Dave loves gadgets. He's got his whole house wired up to his phone. He can turn his sprinklers on from his office. Which is funny, because he works in insurance. You wouldn't think an insurance adjuster would be such a tech nerd. He was telling me about this massive claim he was working on for a warehouse fire down by the river... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, starting tasks. Yeah, no, I don't really have a problem getting started on things. If it's on my plate, I just jump in.
Do you think your mistakes on the sales reports are because you're not paying close enough attention to the details or because you're having trouble understanding the information itself?

Honestly, it's definitely not that I don't understand the information. I know the sales process backward and forward. It's just that I keep making these really dumb mistakes. Like, I'll be looking right at the team dashboard and somehow I'll just copy the wrong numbers over. 

Speaking of the dashboard, they actually just updated the interface on it last week, and it is terrible. They changed the color scheme from this nice, readable blue to like... neon orange and dark grey. It looks like a Halloween decoration. The guys on my team were complaining about it all morning. My buddy Dave in marketing said it was part of some corporate rebranding effort, but I don't know who approved it. Dave hates it too, but he's been super distracted lately anyway because he's trying to buy a boat. He found this old pontoon boat up on the lake that needs a ton of work. I told him he's crazy. You know what they say about boats, right? A hole in the water you throw money into. My uncle had a boat when I was a kid, and the motor blew out the second time we took it out. We were stranded out near the dam for like four hours in the blistering heat. We finally had to flag down this guy in a tiny little aluminum fishing dinghy to tow us back to the marina, and my uncle was so embarrassed he barely spoke the whole ride back...

Wait, sorry. The sales reports. Right. Yeah, it's not the understanding part. It's just the details. I'll miss a whole line in a procedure I was supposed to check off, or I'll swap two numbers, even when I swear I just went over it and double-checked my work. That's actually the main reason I came in to see you, to be honest. I just can't seem to stop making these careless errors.
Do you think your brain is processing the information from the sales reports correctly, or is it more like you're just not catching the mistakes when you review them?

I think... well, it's definitely the second one. I'm processing it fine, I just... I'm not catching them. Like I was saying, that's really the whole reason I'm here. I just keep making these completely dumb mistakes on the sales reports. I'll look right at the team dashboard and somehow copy down the wrong numbers, or I'll totally miss a line in a procedure I'm supposed to check off. And the crazy thing is, I'll think I went over it. I'll review it and think it's perfect, but the errors are still there. 

It's kind of like when you're reading a book and you read the same paragraph three times but you don't actually absorb a single word of it. I was trying to read this sci-fi novel my brother recommended last week—he's super into that hard sci-fi stuff, like the books with actual orbital mechanics and all that. He actually wanted to go to school for aerospace engineering, but he ended up getting a job managing a logistics hub for a trucking company instead. He says it's basically the same thing, just moving boxes on highways instead of in orbit. The trucking industry is wild right now, though. He was telling me they have these new trucks that are practically self-driving on the interstates. They have all these sensors and radar systems. It's like something out of one of those movies where the machines take over. Remember that movie with the killer semi-trucks? Maximum Overdrive, I think it was called? Emilio Estevez was in it. My dad let me watch it when I was way too young, probably like eight years old. I was terrified of garbage trucks for a solid month after that...

Wait, sorry. The mistakes. Yeah, so I'm processing the information fine, I just... I'm missing the careless errors when I review my work. Even when I swear I checked it.

Do you think your mistakes on the sales reports are because you're not paying close enough attention to the details or because you have trouble retaining the information long enough to accurately report it?

I mean, it's definitely not that I can't retain it. I know what the numbers are supposed to be. It's exactly what I've been saying, it's just... I'm not paying close enough attention to the details, I guess. That's why I'm here. I keep making these really dumb mistakes on the sales reports, like just copying the completely wrong numbers right off the team dashboard, or I'll miss a whole line in a procedure I'm supposed to check. And I swear I went over it. 

It's so frustrating because I know the job. I've been doing this since right after high school. Well, not this exact job, I started in the warehouse, actually. Driving a forklift. I loved driving the forklift. It's like a big go-kart. We used to have races on the night shift when the floor manager wasn't around. My buddy Steve was the undisputed champion until he clipped a pallet of printer paper and it just exploded everywhere. We spent three hours cleaning up thousands of sheets of white paper before the morning shift got in. Steve works in real estate now, which is crazy to me. He's always posting these glossy photos of houses on Facebook. He tried to sell me a house last year, actually, but the interest rates are just insane right now. Who can afford a seven percent mortgage? My parents bought their first house for like, thirty grand back in the day, and they thought that was expensive...

But yeah, anyway, the sales reports. It's not that I can't remember the information. I just... I don't know, I just miss the details and make these careless errors even when I think I'm doing it right.
Do you think you would understand the sales reports better if someone explained them to you in a different way?

No, honestly, I don't think someone explaining it differently would help at all. Like I've been saying, I understand the reports just fine. It's really just... I'm missing the details. That's the whole reason I made this appointment. I just keep making these completely dumb mistakes, like I'll look right at the team dashboard and somehow write down the wrong numbers, or I'll completely skip a line on a procedure checklist. And the worst part is, I'll think I went over it perfectly. 

It's kind of like when you're putting together IKEA furniture, right? You look at the diagram, you think you've got it, and then an hour later you realize you put the back panel on upside down and you have to take the whole thing apart. I did that with a bookshelf last month. The instructions are just pictures, no words, which you'd think would be easier, but it's actually worse. My wife was so mad because we had company coming over and there were just dowels and screws all over the living room floor. We ended up just throwing a blanket over the pile and pretending it was a dog bed. We don't even have a dog. We used to have a golden retriever when we first got married, Buster, but he had to go live with my in-laws because our apartment didn't allow pets over thirty pounds. He was a great dog, though. He used to try to catch bees in the backyard...

But yeah, the reports. It's not the explanation. I just keep making those careless errors, missing lines and copying the wrong numbers, even when I'm trying to be careful.
Do you think your mistakes on the sales reports are more because you're not focusing on the details or because you're having trouble with the information itself?

I mean, it's definitely not the information itself. Like I've said, I understand what I'm looking at. It's just the focus thing. I'm just not focusing on the details, and that's exactly what brings me in here. I just keep making these completely dumb mistakes on the sales reports. Like, I'll be looking right at the team dashboard and somehow I'll just copy down the wrong numbers, or I'll totally miss a line in a procedure I was supposed to check off. And the crazy part is, I really thought I went over it. 

It's like when you're driving somewhere you go every day, and suddenly you're pulling into the driveway and you don't even remember the last five miles. Highway hypnosis, they call it. I get that a lot when I drive out to my parents' place. They live out in the country, about forty minutes away. It's all these long, flat farm roads. They grow a lot of corn out there. And soybeans. Did you know soybeans are in basically everything now? I watched this documentary on Netflix about it. They use soy in industrial lubricants, plastics, even the foam in car seats. It's wild how one little bean can do all that. Henry Ford actually built a whole car out of soybean plastic back in the thirties. He took an axe to the trunk to prove how strong it was. I saw a picture of it online. I wonder why that never caught on? Probably the oil companies shutting it down. You know how those big corporations are, always buying up patents and burying them so they can keep selling petroleum... 

Wait, what was I... right, the reports. Yeah, so it's not the information. I just keep making these careless errors, copying wrong numbers and missing lines, even when I thought I checked it perfectly.

No, honestly, I don't think someone explaining it differently would help at all. Like I've been saying, I understand the reports just fine. It's really just... I'm missing the details. That's the whole reason I made this appointment. I just keep making these completely dumb mistakes, like I'll look right at the team dashboard and somehow write down the wrong numbers, or I'll completely skip a line on a procedure checklist. And the worst part is, I'll think I went over it perfectly. 

It's kind of like when you're putting together IKEA furniture, right? You look at the diagram, you think you've got it, and then an hour later you realize you put the back panel on upside down and you have to take the whole thing apart. I did that with a bookshelf last month. The instructions are just pictures, no words, which you'd think would be easier, but it's actually worse. My wife was so mad because we had company coming over and there were just dowels and screws all over the living room floor. We ended up just throwing a blanket over the pile and pretending it was a dog bed. We don't even have a dog. We used to have a golden retriever when we first got married, Buster, but he had to go live with my in-laws because our apartment didn't allow pets over thirty pounds. He was a great dog, though. He used to try to catch bees in the backyard...

But yeah, the reports. It's not the explanation. I just keep making those careless errors, missing lines and copying the wrong numbers, even when I'm trying to be careful.

patient.answer:
I mean, it's definitely not the information itself. Like I've said, I understand what I'm looking at. It's just the focus thing. I'm just not focusing on the details, and that's exactly what brings me in here. I just keep making these completely dumb mistakes on the sales reports. Like, I'll be looking right at the team dashboard and somehow I'll just copy down the wrong numbers, or I'll totally miss a line in a procedure I was supposed to check off. And the crazy part is, I really thought I went over it. 

It's like when you're driving somewhere you go every day, and suddenly you're pulling into the driveway and you don't even remember the last five miles. Highway hypnosis, they call it. I get that a lot when I drive out to my parents' place. They live out in the country, about forty minutes away. It's all these long, flat farm roads. They grow a lot of corn out there. And soybeans. Did you know soybeans are in basically everything now? I watched this documentary on Netflix about it. They use soy in industrial lubricants, plastics, even the foam in car seats. It's wild how one little bean can do all that. Henry Ford actually built a whole car out of soybean plastic back in the thirties. He took an axe to the trunk to prove how strong it was. I saw a picture of it online. I wonder why that never caught on? Probably the oil companies shutting it down. You know how those big corporations are, always buying up patents and burying them so they can keep selling petroleum... 

Wait, what was I... right, the reports. Yeah, so it's not the information. I just keep making these careless errors, copying wrong numbers and missing lines, even when I thought I checked it perfectly.
